predecessors.name: Kingdom of Kartli
predecessors.text: Kartli, Teimuraz II's kingdom from 1744: 'After Teimuraz II's death in 1762, Irakli II assumed control over Kartli'

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Kakheti
predecessors.text: Kakheti, Heraclius II's own kingdom until the union

successors.name: Russian Empire
successors.text: the whole kingdom: Alexander I 'proceeded to confirm annexation' on 12 September 1801

ledger.x: 1762: Heraclius II unites Kartli and Kakheti.

1762: Kakheti is absorbed into the united kingdom ('the unification of the two eastern Georgian kingdoms'); the Kartli page footnote has Teimuraz II ruling Kakheti 1732-44 and Kartli 1744-62, and the union page names no earlier Kakheti king for Heraclius.
8 September 1795: Agha Mohammad Khan fights for Tbilisi.
Late September 1795: the Qajar army leaves.

wars.name: Qajar invasion of Georgia
wars.outcome: Qajar victory at Krtsanisi (8-11 September 1795): 'The Georgians had lost 4,000 men in the battle, the Iranians 13,000'; Tbilisi was sacked and some 15,000 captives taken.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier: the Treaty of Georgievsk (24 July 1783) 'guaranteed its territorial integrity' without defining the borders, and no page opened names any khanate as tributary to the kingdom (the Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti page…
